project.title: Integrated Home Care Safety and Hygiene Improvement Pilot
project.objective: Design and pilot a standardized safety and hygiene routine for home care visits, with clear checklists, training, and monitoring across selected clients.
deliverables: Standardized home visit safety and hygiene checklist
Client-specific care and dietary instruction sheets
Home care aide training mini-guide on safe work practices
Household supplies and equipment stocking plan
Pilot evaluation report with incident and compliance summary
constraints: Pilot must be designed and ready to start within 21 days
Procedures must comply with basic health and safety regulations
New routines must fit within existing visit time slots
No additional full-time staff can be hired for the pilot
Supplies budget for the pilot is capped and must be tracked

risks.risk: Home care aides may see the new checklist as extra admin and skip steps.
risks.mitigation: Keep checklist short, co-design with aides, and explain time-saving benefits during training.

risks.risk: Households may lack space or willingness to store extra hygiene supplies.
risks.mitigation: Create a minimal core kit and an optional extended kit; confirm storage options with families first.

risks.risk: Supply items for the pilot may be out of stock or delayed.
risks.mitigation: Define primary and backup items, and coordinate early with shelf fillers on substitutions.

risks.risk: New cleaning or disinfection products may cause allergies or sensitivities.
risks.mitigation: Chemistry technicians review product safety sheets and define safe-use and allergy-check steps.

themes.why_relevant: Core of the project; defines what aides actually do in each home visit.
Without the right products and tools, new routines cannot be followed reliably.
Dietary and product sensitivities must be respected to avoid incidents.
New process only works if aides understand and accept it in daily work.
Tracking issues and near-misses is needed to refine the routine after the pilot.

backlog.task: Draft a concise home visit safety and hygiene checklist for pilot clients
definition_of_done: Checklist covers cleaning, disinfection, linen handling, and basic first aid readiness
Checklist limited to one page and grouped by visit phase
Reviewed by at least one home care aide for practicality
Version 1.0 stored and shared as official pilot document

backlog.task: Create client-specific care and dietary instruction sheets
definition_of_done: Instruction sheet template created with sections for diet, allergies, mobility, and routines
At least five pilot clients have completed sheets based on existing knowledge
Sheets validated with client or family representative where possible
Sheets stored in a shared location and linked to the checklist

backlog.task: Review and approve safe cleaning and disinfection products list
definition_of_done: List includes 3–5 core products with clear usage instructions
Safety and allergy considerations documented for each product
Products checked for compatibility with common household surfaces
List shared with shelf fillers for availability confirmation

backlog.task: Define a minimal home care hygiene kit and restocking rules
definition_of_done: Kit contents defined with product codes and acceptable substitutes
Restocking frequency and trigger levels documented
Kit cost estimated and within budget constraints
Process for reporting stock-outs agreed with home care aides

backlog.task: Prepare a short training guideline for aides on the new routine
definition_of_done: Guideline explains why changes are needed and key safety points
Includes simple examples of correct and incorrect practices
Reviewed by one home care aide for clarity and tone
Final version shared in the channel before pilot start

backlog.task: Pilot the checklist and instruction sheets with selected clients
definition_of_done: At least five clients included in the pilot over two weeks
Checklist used in every visit for pilot clients
Any incidents or near-misses logged using the incident template
Initial feedback from aides and clients captured

backlog.task: Set up a simple incident and near-miss logging process
definition_of_done: Incident template created with fields for type, cause, and follow-up
Logging process explained in the training guideline
Storage location for logs agreed and accessible to the team
Test entry created to confirm process works

backlog.task: Align supply placement and labeling in storage areas used by aides
definition_of_done: Shelves or storage areas mapped for pilot supplies
Labels created and placed for each product in the hygiene kit
Out-of-stock alert method agreed with aides
Before/after photos or notes captured for reference

backlog.task: Collect and summarize pilot feedback and incident data
definition_of_done: All incident logs from pilot period reviewed and categorized
Feedback from at least two aides and two families summarized
Key issues and improvement ideas listed
Summary shared in the channel ahead of the wrap-up discussion

backlog.task: Adjust checklist and instruction sheets based on pilot results
definition_of_done: Top 5 improvement points from pilot addressed in updated documents
Revised versions validated by one chemistry technician
Changes clearly highlighted for easy re-training
Updated documents stored and old versions archived

backlog.task: Confirm final supply list and stocking plan for wider rollout
definition_of_done: Supply list updated based on pilot learnings and substitutions used
Stocking plan adjusted to avoid frequent shortages
Any cost changes noted and shared with stakeholders
Plan approved by project stakeholders in the channel

backlog.task: Compile final pilot evaluation report and recommendations
definition_of_done: Report includes objectives, approach, results, and key metrics
Recommendations for rollout and further improvements listed
Report references updated checklist, instructions, and supply plan
Report shared in the channel and ready for stakeholder review

threads_plan.thread_goal: Align on pilot scope, client selection, and overall approach.
threads_plan.trigger: Kickoff message announcing the safety and hygiene improvement pilot.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Confirm the list of pilot clients and visit schedule to include in A8.
Agree on the final scope of the checklist items for A1 before drafting.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Design and finalize the safety checklist and training materials.
threads_plan.trigger: First draft of the home visit checklist shared for comments.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve version 1.0 of the Home Visit Safety and Hygiene Checklist (A1).
Approve the training mini-guide (A3) and confirm training format.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Lock in supply list, hygiene kit contents, and storage setup.
threads_plan.trigger: Shelf filler shares proposed hygiene kit and storage plan.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve the final hygiene kit contents and restocking rules (A4).
Agree on storage locations and labeling approach using A7.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Coordinate pilot execution, incident logging, and quick fixes.
threads_plan.trigger: Start of the pilot period with aides using the new checklist.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Confirm how and when aides must log incidents using A5 during the pilot.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Review pilot results and agree on adjustments and rollout plan.
threads_plan.trigger: Chemistry technician posts the pilot evaluation summary draft.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve final recommendations in the evaluation report (A6) and go/no-go for wider rollout.

channel_rituals: Async daily check-in during the pilot where aides post quick updates on visits and any incidents.
Weekly planning message to confirm supply needs and restocking actions for the coming week.
Mid-pilot review thread to capture early feedback and decide on small adjustments.
End-of-pilot retrospective thread to discuss what worked, what did not, and next steps.
